summary: Hunhun, the Concord's horsemen: a riders' moot and its Horse-Lord, herds and remounts, the great ride and a saddle charter.

riders_moot.name: The Riders' Moot
riders_moot.desc: The brotherhoods elect their Horse-Lord in the open air at midsummer.

riders_moot_2.name: The Horse-Lord's Law
riders_moot_2.desc: The Horse-Lord's judgements are written down and kept in a saddlebag.

great_herds.name: Herds of Hunhun
great_herds.desc: Herds grazing from horizon to horizon, counted in thousands.

great_herds_2.name: Wealth on Hooves
great_herds_2.desc: Herds, remounts, escorts and saddlers make Hunhun rich.

escort_companies_spirit.name: Escort Companies
escort_companies_spirit.desc: Quick, loyal and expensive riders escort the merchants of the lake roads.

scouting_ride.name: The Scouting Ride
scouting_ride.desc: Riders range far ahead of the line and return with the freshest news.

riding_drills_spirit.name: Riding Drills
riding_drills_spirit.desc: The brotherhoods wheel, feint and charge as one.

riding_drills_2.name: Swift as Wind
riding_drills_2.desc: A hundred miles between dawn and dusk, with fresh horses at every halt.

ride_captains_spirit.name: The Ride-Captains
ride_captains_spirit.desc: The captains sit in council and have never lost an argument about horses.

free_riders.name: Lords of Horses
free_riders.desc: No crown, charter or king can command a free ride.

the_long_ride_spirit.name: The Long Ride
the_long_ride_spirit.desc: Every brotherhood is saddled, and the horn has sounded.

a_quarrel_over_grazing.title: A Quarrel over Grazing
a_quarrel_over_grazing.desc: Two brotherhoods have driven their herds onto the same stretch of grass, and neither will give way. The Horse-Lord may judge between them from the saddle, or let the ride-captains race for it as their grandfathers did.

options.name: Let the ride-captains race for it.

deliverers_tents.title: The Deliverer's Tents
deliverers_tents.desc: Almoners of the Deliverer have raised tents at the great gathering and are offering bread and linen to all who come. The riders are curious, and a little suspicious of anyone who gives something for nothing.

remount_contracts.title: Remount Contracts
remount_contracts.desc: The riders of Hunhun have delivered another year's remounts to the Royal Army, and the treasury must decide whether to settle the account on time. The riders will remember either answer.

focuses.name: The Riders' Moot
focuses.desc: The brotherhoods of Hunhun meet in the open air at midsummer and elect a Horse-Lord from among their ride-captains. The chair is a saddle on a stump, and nobody has proposed improving it.

focuses.name: Elect the Ride-Captains
focuses.desc: Each brotherhood chooses its own captain by a race over the old course, and the captains choose the Horse-Lord. The method has the virtue of being unarguable.

focuses.name: The Open Grass
focuses.desc: The grass belongs to the brotherhoods, and the brotherhoods quarrel over every acre of it. The Horse-Lord rides out each spring to settle the worst of the disputes before they become feuds.

focuses.name: The Horse-Lord's Law
focuses.desc: The Horse-Lord's judgements are written down and kept in a saddlebag, so that they may be cited by the next. It is the nearest thing Hunhun has to a law.

focuses.name: The Temple Tents
focuses.desc: Almoners have begun to put up tents at the riders' gatherings, with bread, linen and a place to tend the sick. The riders are curious, if not yet convinced.

focuses.name: One Ride, One Lord
focuses.desc: The brotherhoods agree to ride as one when the Horse-Lord sounds the horn. It is not a crown, and no rider would call it one, but it does the work of one.

focuses.name: Herds of Hunhun
focuses.desc: The herds of Hunhun graze the open grass from one horizon to the next. The riders count them in thousands and the Golden Court counts them in coin.

focuses.name: Remount Contracts
focuses.desc: The Royal Army buys its remounts from Hunhun and pays late. The riders laugh at that over beer and remember every debt.

focuses.name: Saddleries
focuses.desc: Saddlers, bit-makers and harness-wrights set up beside the herds. A Hunhun saddle is made to last a rider's lifetime and his horse's.

focuses.name: Horse Roads
focuses.desc: Broad tracks of beaten earth cross the grass between the horse-fairs. They are not paved, but a herd can move along them without breaking its legs.

focuses.name: Escort Companies
focuses.desc: Companies of riders are hired to escort merchants on the lake roads. They are quick, loyal and expensive, and merchants who skimp tend to be robbed.

focuses.name: Wealth on Hooves
focuses.desc: Herds, remounts, escorts and saddlers together make Hunhun the wealthiest country of the open grass. The riders do not boast of it, and pay their debts early.

focuses.name: The Riders of Hunhun
focuses.desc: The riders of Hunhun are the fastest in the Middle Lands. They live on horseback, sleep in the saddle and treat walking as an affliction.

focuses.name: Horse Archery
focuses.desc: Hunhun's riders loose from the saddle at a full gallop, three shafts for every breath of the horse. A host of them is a storm that moves.

focuses.name: The Scouting Ride
focuses.desc: The crown's marches are scouted by Hunhun riders, who range far ahead of the line and return with news that is days fresher than anyone else's.

focuses.name: Heavy Riders
focuses.desc: The Horse-Lord's own riders wear mail and carry lances. They are slower than their cousins and a good deal harder to stop.

focuses.name: Riding Drills
focuses.desc: The brotherhoods drill together on the open grass, learning to wheel, feint and charge as one. The first drill is chaos; the tenth is poetry.

focuses.name: Swift as Wind
focuses.desc: The riders of Hunhun are taught to cover a hundred miles between dawn and dusk, with fresh horses at every halt. The wind itself seems to follow behind.

focuses.name: The Ride-Captains
focuses.desc: The ride-captains are given a standing place in the Horse-Lord's council, with a say in the choice of the field. They have never lost an argument about horses.

focuses.name: The Great Ride
focuses.desc: Once in a generation the brotherhoods muster for the Great Ride, a progress of ten thousand horses around the rim of the grass. The sound of it is heard across three states.

focuses.name: The Saddle Charter
focuses.desc: The charter that made Hunhun a dominion was signed in the saddle, and the parchment still smells of horse. The riders honour it as long as the debts are paid.

focuses.name: Riders for the Royal Army
focuses.desc: Hunhun lends its riders to the Royal Army as scouts and skirmishers. They come on their own horses and wear their own cloaks, and they do not always salute.

focuses.name: The Old Freedoms of the Ride
focuses.desc: The Horse-Lord reads aloud the old freedoms of the ride, which the charter does not mention. He asks Parim to restore them in a Free Charter, and Parim is unlikely to oblige.

focuses.name: Scouts for the Lost Cause
focuses.desc: Hunhun's scouts join the Lost Cause's frontier companies and ride the southern road. They are paid late, as always, but they do not complain.

focuses.name: Riders of the Free Dominions
focuses.desc: With the Golden King dead, the riders of Hunhun cast in their lot with the dominions who would have their charters back. They have always ridden where they pleased.

focuses.name: Lords of Horses, Not of Men
focuses.desc: The riders say that they are lords of horses and not of men, and that no crown, charter or king can command a free ride. Whoever rules Parim, the grass is Hunhun's.

focuses.name: The Long Ride
focuses.desc: The horn sounds over the open grass, and every brotherhood saddles up. The riders of Hunhun have been waiting for this ride, and they intend to make it count.

focuses.name: Harry the Invaders
focuses.desc: Hunhun's riders strike at the flanks and rear of the invader, in small bands that appear and vanish. The enemy never finds the same riders twice.

focuses.name: Riders at the Crossings
focuses.desc: Every ford and bridge on the lake roads is held by a company of riders. A host that crosses will have to do it under their bows.

focuses.name: Ride with the Heir
focuses.desc: The Heir has returned, and Hunhun's fastest riders carry the word to every brotherhood. Within a fortnight the grass is empty of horses.

focuses.name: Home to the Grass
focuses.desc: The war is over, and the riders come home to the open grass. They stable their horses, mend their saddles and settle, at last, their quarrels over grazing.
